acceptanceCriteria.text: Submitting the first non-empty user question automatically replaces a new generic chat title with a short, meaningful title derived from that question, without interrupting submission.
The title appears in sidebar/header without restart and persists when reopening the chat and restarting the app.
Later turns do not continually rename the chat; manually chosen or creation-supplied titles, including meaningful run/Kanban titles, are preserved and win rename races.
Blank input, startup/system text, assistant/tool output and unrelated terminal input do not name chats.
Behavioral regression tests, applicable delivery checks and real desktop smoke evidence cover naming, persistence and manual-title protection.

body:
## Outcome
After the person submits the first real question/prompt in a new chat, automatically replace its generic title with a short, meaningful title derived from that question. Show the persisted title in the sidebar and chat header without a restart. This is card creation only, not authorization to execute it.

## Behavior and boundaries
Name a generic, untitled chat once from its first non-empty user question; do not rename on every subsequent turn. Preserve a title supplied at creation or manually chosen by the person, including a manual rename racing automatic naming. Preserve meaningful epic/run/Kanban chat titles. Blank input, CLI startup text, system instructions, tool output and assistant responses must not supply the title. Normal prompt submission must continue unchanged. No new external naming service, credentials or paid API dependency is required.

## Source locations
- `src/main/agents/chatRecords.ts`: `createChatRecords` exposes `renameChat` and already persists titles through `store.updateChat`; reuse the existing storage path, with automatic eligibility checked against current persisted state.
- `src/main/agents/chatHandlers.ts`: existing `renameChat` and `chatsChanged` provide the rename/event path; preserve folder authorization, validation and event-driven updates.
- `src/main/agents/chatStore.ts`: existing chat persistence; inspect existing title/default handling before deciding whether title-origin metadata is needed.
- `src/shared/agents/chat.ts`: persisted chat schema; only extend if necessary to distinguish automatic/default and human titles, maintaining compatibility with stored chats.
- `src/renderer/src/agents/useChats.ts`: `useChatEvents` reloads lists when chat events arrive, and `useChats` exposes manual rename. Ensure sidebar/header reflect automatic changes through existing events.
- `src/renderer/src/agents/TerminalPane.tsx` and `useTerminal.ts`: terminal-backed chat surface and lifecycle. Verified investigation entry points, not proof of a semantic first-prompt event. Locate the actual submitted user-message/session integration before implementing; never infer user questions from arbitrary PTY bytes or terminal output (shell commands, passwords and control sequences are not chat questions).
- Extend `src/main/agents/chatRecords.test.ts` and `src/renderer/src/agents/useChats.test.tsx` where applicable. Add policy tests beside the eventual naming implementation, following neighboring test conventions; exact new file placement depends on the verified prompt-ingestion owner.

## Tests
Write failing behavioral tests before implementation: first genuine non-empty user question names a default chat; later questions do not continually rename it; supplied/manual titles and a concurrent manual rename win; non-user/startup/blank content is ignored; generated title persists and event-driven list refresh displays it. Test observable behavior, not wiring/source strings.

## Verification
Exercise a real desktop chat: submit a question, observe automatic sidebar/header naming, reopen/restart and verify persistence, then manually rename and send another question to verify the manual title remains. Check a pre-named Kanban/run chat is unchanged. Run targeted regression tests and the full standalone delivery gate (lint, npm test, applicable Fireguard, typecheck, deadcode, build); record environmental limitations without suppressing failures. Update existing chat documentation with the one-time naming rule.
expectedArtifacts: Automatic first-question title policy integrated with the verified user-message owner and existing chat persistence/events
Behavioral regression tests and desktop verification evidence
title: Automatically name a new chat after the first user question
